Portend

por-TEND · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To portend is to be a sign or warning that something, especially something important or bad, will happen.

A single hairline crack spreading slowly across the dam's concrete wall seemed to portend a catastrophic flood downstream.

Worked Example

The sudden silence in the forest -- no birdsong, no rustling leaves -- portended a predator somewhere close by.

Portend is almost always used for something threatening or significant on the horizon, not for good news or small events.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

foreshadow: to indicate that something will happen in the future

presage: to be a sign that something, often bad, will happen

Where it sits · how strongly the future is signaled — suggest → portend → prophesy

suggest vs. portend: To suggest something is only to hint at a possibility, a much softer signal than an omen that portends disaster.

prophesy vs. portend: To prophesy something is to declare with confidence, often through mystical or religious insight, that it will happen -- a far stronger claim than merely portending it.

Build the Word

The pieces

prefix — por-

prefix — por-: forth, forward (a form of Latin pro-) (Latin)

root — tend

root — tend: to stretch (Latin tendere)

Put it together

Put it together: Portend combines por- ('forth,' from Latin pro-) with tend (Latin tendere, 'to stretch') -- literally 'to stretch forth,' which came to mean signaling or foreshadowing something before it happens.

Use the root in a new word: extend

Use the root in a new word: extend: The city council voted to extend the library's hours through the entire summer.
